item.title: Two enduring controversies in de Quervain surgery: retinacular repair and accessory abductor pollicis longus tendon excision
item.description: CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports adequate decompression and recognition of anatomical variation rather than a single mandatory technique. The available evidence does not justify routine retinacular reconstruction or routine accessory tendon excision in all patients; both may be considered selectively according to intraoperative findings.

item.title: Clinical factors associated with coercive behavioral interventions in psychiatric inpatients: A prospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Baseline assessment and ongoing monitoring may help identify patients at greater likelihood of subsequent CBIs. Attention to negative symptoms and resistance, with structured, empathic engagement, may support safer, patient-centered care.

item.title: Haginin A suppresses oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory mediators via MAPK and inflammasome regulation in LPS-stimulated microglia
item.description: Haginin A (HA), a flavonoid isolated from Lespedeza cyrtobotrya, has been reported to possess various biological activities; however, its anti-neuroinflammatory activity has not been clarified yet. In this study, we investigated the effect of HA on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammatory response in microglia. HA treatment significantly reduced nitric oxide (NO), and inflammation-inducing cytokines including tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α and interleukin (IL)-6, in LPS-stimulated BV2...

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Interferometric Near-Field Scanning Optical Microscopy via Phase Conjugation of a Multimode Fiber Probe
item.description: Interferometric near-field scanning optical microscopy (NSOM) enables simultaneous measurement of both the amplitude and phase of the optical near field. In its aperture-type implementation, the local field is collected through a sub-wavelength aperture and an optical fiber. The choice of this fiber imposes an inherent trade-off between signal strength and phase fidelity. Single-mode fiber probes maintain phase fidelity but suffer from low signal intensity, whereas multimode fiber probes offer...

item.title: A Preliminary Study of Mobile-Based CBT for Anger Management in Individuals With ASD Without Intellectual Disability
item.description: This study examined the preliminary efficacy of HARU ASD, a mobile-based cognitive behavioral therapy program (mCBT), for anger management in adolescents and young adults with autism spectrum disorder without intellectual disability. Thirty participants (intervention group n = 16, waitlist control group n = 14) and twenty-five caregivers (intervention group n = 14, waitlist control group n = 11) were included in the final analysis. Self-report, caregiver-proxy questionnaires (9 subscales each),...

item.title: Postpandemic Social Contact Patterns: A Cross-Sectional Survey in Japan, South Korea, Thailand, and Vietnam
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Contact frequencies in Japan and South Korea remained below prepandemic levels in 2025, suggesting persistent postpandemic changes in mixing behavior. Evidence for comparable changes in Thailand and Vietnam was inconclusive. Future surveys should collect setting-specific information, in addition to contact frequency and age, to clarify how changes in work, education, and household interaction shape postpandemic social mixing patterns.

item.title: Prediabetes subtype-based stratification reveals distinct long-term risks for type 2 diabetes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Diabetes progression differs based on both glycaemic subtype and physiological subtype. Integrating IGI and ISI with conventional definitions enhances risk stratification and may help to identify high-risk individuals for earlier targeted intervention.

item.title: Performance of large language models in pediatric infectious disease education: a multi-condition comparative study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Current LLMs performed highly in structured, expert-reviewed PID scenarios and may assist with information organization and early-stage clinical reasoning. However, their optimal use remains within clinician-supervised workflows, where AI-generated outputs complement, rather than replace, human clinical judgment.

item.title: Final analysis results from DREAMM-3, a phase 3 study of belantamab mafodotin versus pomalidomide plus dexamethasone in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma
item.description: No abstract

item.title: AI-derived panoramic score and its association with major systemic diseases: A retrospective cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: An AI-derived panoramic radiograph-based score was independently associated with five selected systemic diagnoses. Clinical significance An AI-derived score obtained from routinely acquired panoramic radiographs was independently associated with major systemic diseases. This automated, quantitative score may serve as an exploratory image-based index, supporting integrated management between dental and medical care.

item.title: Ezetimibe pretreatment attenuates early ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model of lung transplantation
item.description: Ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) after transplantation causes early and late graft dysfunction. Ezetimibe (Eze) is a lipid-reducing agent that has been reported to attenuate oxidative stress and inflammation in non-pulmonary models of ischemia-reperfusion. We examined its effect in a rat lung transplantation model. Lewis rats (n = 8/group) underwent left lung transplantation without pretreatment (LT) or with Eze pretreatment of the donor (LT-D), recipient (LT-R), or both (LT-DR). Eze (1 mg/kg)...

item.title: Flexible and stretchable bioelectronics for sports wearable monitoring: Materials, Device Engineering, and Intelligent Wearable Platforms
item.description: Modern sports science is undergoing a paradigm shift from subjective coaching to objective, data-driven precision training. Consequently, wearable electronics for acquiring precise data during sports activities are attracting attention. However, conventional rigid wearables inherently suffer from mechanical mismatches between rigid wearables and the soft, deformable human skin, inducing severe motion artifacts and restricting natural biomechanics during high-intensity athletic activities. To...

item.title: Effects of treadmill exercise with and without vertical traction on gait, pain, disability, trunk proprioception, and depression in patients with chronic mechanical low back pain: A randomized controlled trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Adding vertical traction and partial body weight support to treadmill exercise may provide additional benefits for gait performance, disability, and trunk repositioning accuracy in patients with CMLBP. Interpretation is limited by the small sample size and the inability to distinguish the effects of vertical unloading from those of harness support.

item.title: Nanotechnology-driven cryopreservation across cells and 3D constructs
item.description: Cryopreservation is essential for cell-based research, regenerative medicine, and emerging therapies; however, conventional strategies remain limited by ice-induced damage, osmotic imbalance, and cryoprotectant (CPA)-associated toxicity. This review discusses the mechanisms of cryoinjury, limitations of conventional CPA-based strategies, and emerging approaches, including combinatorial CPA formulations and ice-modulating agents such as antifreeze proteins and synthetic ice recrystallization...

item.title: Unrevealing biofouling in a solar-powered membrane distillation process operated with intermittent mode
item.description: Fouling in membrane distillation processes has been investigated primarily in terms of inorganic scaling under continuous operating conditions. This study investigated biofouling in a solar-powered membrane distillation (SPMD) process operated in intermittent mode to simulate the sustainable operation of an MD system coupled with renewable energy. The intermittent SPMD process was evaluated at feed temperatures of 25 and 55 °C using two membrane types, polytetrafluoroethylene...

item.title: Corrigendum to "Criterion validity of brief, comprehensive, and latent measures of intrinsic capacity against frailty, disability, and mortality in older adults" [J Nutr Health Aging, 30 (2026) 101002]
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Post-Diagnosis Depression and Suicide Risk Among Cancer Survivors: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Depression arising after cancer diagnosis was strongly associated with suicide risk in this nationwide cohort and represents a clinically relevant marker of suicide risk among cancer survivors, supporting the integration of systematic mental health assessment into routine oncology care.

item.title: pH-Driven Two-Stage Conformational Switching Activates an Acid-Responsive Chaperone
item.description: Acidification rapidly denatures bacterial periplasmic proteins, yet this compartment lacks ATP-dependent chaperones. We identify AchC as an acid-responsive, ATP-independent chaperone crucial for acid tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. As proton influx across the outer membrane leaves insufficient time for transcriptional or translational adaptation, AchC is activated post-translationally. We reveal that AchC is activated by precisely tuned, conformational transitions driven by pH changes. At...

item.title: Tumor-related local complications as a major contributor to mortality after definitive radiotherapy for unresectable extrahepatic bile duct cancer
item.description: CONCLUSION: Definitive radiotherapy provided favorable local control with acceptable toxicity in unresectable extrahepatic bile duct cancer. Although distant metastasis was the predominant failure pattern, local complications accounted for at least 40% of deaths, supporting continued efforts to optimize local treatment alongside emerging systemic therapies.

item.title: Relative muscle mass and grip strength as complementary correlates of metabolic syndrome: a nationwide DXA-based study of Korean adults
item.description: CONCLUSION: ASM/BW showed more consistent associations with MetS across the sensitivity analyses performed than relative HGS, although associations differed by normalization method, the optimal choice of which remains uncertain. Because the design is cross-sectional, these findings indicate association only and require prospective validation before clinical application.

item.title: Subfoveal choroidal thickness across age and sex in a Korean population: insights from KNHANES 2017-2021
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a comprehensive normative reference framework for SFCT utilizing a nationally representative Korean population. These data may serve as reference values for evaluating choroidal structural changes in retinal and choroidal diseases.

item.title: Pediatric chronological age estimation from pelvic radiographs using deep learning: a multicenter retrospective study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Automated age estimation in children is feasible from pelvic radiography using a deep neural network.

item.title: Sleep Quality in Adults with Cancer: Associations with Symptom Burden and Psychological Resilience
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Poor sleep was common among adults with cancer. Mental health and resilience were independently associated with sleep quality beyond clinical characteristics. These findings highlight the relevance of considering psychosocial factors alongside clinical characteristics when assessing sleep problems in supportive oncology care.

item.title: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Working Memory Enhancement: A Comparative Study of Electrical and Ultrasound Stimulation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: taVNS can acutely enhance working memory performance, and U-taVNS may offer a comparable, better-tolerated alternative to E-taVNS. Our findings highlight the potential of taVNS to support memory function, while showing the importance of further research to clarify modality-specific effects and to optimize stimulation parameters.

item.title: Use of an AI metabolomics score to predict cardiovascular risk among patients with Psoriasis in the MGB and UK Biobanks
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the potential of AI-driven metabolomics to refine cardiovascular risk prediction in immune-mediated diseases and enable precision prevention strategies for patients with psoriasis.

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Adjuvant Systemic Therapies After Nephrectomy for Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis and Multi-Criteria Benefit-Risk Assessment
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Adding belzutifan to pembrolizumab improved disease-free survival but increased toxicity and treatment discontinuation. The decision analysis illustrates a model-dependent trade-off rather than identifying a preferred regimen. Because overall survival data are immature, the decision to intensify treatment remains risk and preference sensitive.

item.title: Glycyrrhizic acid alters [<sup>99m</sup>Tc]Tc-PSMA biodistribution and tumour progression in a DMBA-induced breast cancer model
item.description: Breast cancer remains a major global health challenge, and understanding interactions between pharmacological agents and radiopharmaceuticals is important for interpreting molecular imaging findings. Glycyrrhizic acid (GA), a bioactive triterpenoid derived from Glycyrrhiza glabra, has reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities; however, its effects on PSMA-targeted radiotracer biodistribution remain poorly investigated. This study evaluated GA effects on tumour-related biological...

item.title: Impact of oxidative degradation on the bioavailability of subcutaneously administered adalimumab
item.description: Subcutaneous (SC) administration of therapeutic antibodies enhances patient convenience and healthcare resource efficiency compared to intravenous (IV) delivery, but therapy can be limited by incomplete bioavailability (BA) of SC biotherapeutics. This limitation may be attributed to processes inherent to the unique composition of SC tissue, including the potential presence of reactive oxygen species (ROS) within the SC microenvironment, which can induce chemical and structural instability and...

item.title: Investigating fatigability and cortical activation during prolonged foot tapping in multiple sclerosis
item.description: People with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) often exhibit motor fatigability and reduced foot-tapping ability. However, the coupling between performance and cortical activity during fast, repetitive and prolonged ankle movements remains unexplored. We aimed to investigate the neural correlates of a prolonged foot-tap task (FTT) in pwMS and healthy controls (HC). Thirty-nine pwMS (EDSS 4[3.5], 55[14] years) and 18 HC (54.5[9.75) years) performed one 1-minute FTT for each foot. Wearable sensors and...

item.title: A Mechanistic Learning Framework for Breast Cancer Relapse Prediction
item.description: Breast cancer recurrence is thought to arise, at least in part, from disseminated tumour cells (DTCs) that may seed distant organs prior to or during surgery, persist in a dormant state for years to decades, and eventually resume proliferation to form clinically detectable metastases. Standard survival models treat this process statistically, without reference to the underlying biological kinetics, and while artificial intelligence (AI) has improved predictive accuracy, its "black-box" nature...

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of turmeric and curcumin formulations on glycemic, lipid, and inflammatory markers in people with prediabetes: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
item.description: Prediabetes is a growing global health concern associated with higher risk of diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Curcumin has been studied for glycemic, lipid, and inflammatory effects, but comparative data across formulations remain limited. This network meta-analysis (NMA) evaluated turmeric and curcumin formulations in adults with prediabetes. Seven databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing turmeric/curcumin formulations with placebo. Primary outcomes...

item.title: Emulsifier Intake in Healthy Controls and Patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study with Longitudinal Follow-Up of Long-Term Outcomes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Intake of emulsifiers, but not UPFs, was higher in IBD patients compared to controls. Although unadjusted analyses suggested an association between higher UPF and emulsifier intake and adverse IBD-related outcomes, neither remained an independent predictor after adjustment for potential confounders, yet larger studies are warranted.

item.title: Manifold view of spinal motor control: A paradigm in motion
item.description: The neural manifold framework has transformed our understanding of cortical motor control, focusing on population dynamics that is constrained to low-dimensional structures in state space, where behaviors correspond to structured trajectories with characteristic topology. Yet the spinal cord, which houses the core circuitry responsible for rhythmic motor output such as walking, has remained largely unexplored from a manifold perspective. For decades, spinal motor function has been interpreted...

item.title: Baseline MRI markers and clinical outcomes during anti-amyloid β therapy: A real-world study in a Japanese dementia center
item.description: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Baseline medial temporal atrophy was associated with functional decline and microbleeds with ARIA-H. Pretreatment MRI may provide prognostic and safety information during anti-amyloid β therapy.

item.title: A theoretical framework for efficient solvent suppression in solid-state NMR: Circumventing solvent-signal refocusing by adiabatic-inversion-based dephasing
item.description: We recently developed a solvent-suppression scheme employing adiabatic-inversion pulses for high-resolution solid-state NMR (SSNMR), termed Solvent suppression of Liquid signal with Adiabatic Pulse (SLAP) [T. Matsunaga et al., J. Biomol. NMR 75, 365 (2021)], and demonstrated its superior performance over the traditional MISSISSIPPI scheme [D.H. Zhou et al., J. Magn. Reson. 192, 162 (2008)]. Here, we present a theoretical framework explaining this advantage. We show that MISSISSIPPI-based...

item.title: When vendor reputation does not matter: Trust decoupling and pragmatic trust in Generative AI adoption among university students
item.description: Trust Transfer Theory predicts that trust in a reputable developer extends to its products, yet this assumption has rarely been tested for non-deterministic generative AI (GenAI) systems. This study examines how trust forms and transfers across conceptual (AI in general), institutional (vendor), and product (specific GenAI tool) levels, and how these trust layers relate to students' adoption intention. Survey data from 480 undergraduate students who actively use GenAI at a public research...

item.title: Prevalence and risk factors for impaired tissue integrity in long-term care settings: A multicenter study
item.description: This multicenter, cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence and characteristics of tissue integrity impairments including pressure injuries (PIs), incontinence-associated dermatitis, skin tears, and medical device-related PIs among older adults residing in long-term care settings in Türkiye, and to identify associated risk factors. multicenter study was conducted across eight public and seven private nursing homes and residential care centers in Ankara and Istanbul. The study...

item.title: Effect modification of maternal concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances on vaccine effectiveness in children up to 6 years of age: The Japan Environment and Children's Study
item.description: Epidemiological evidence suggests that per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure may attenuate antibody responses to vaccination. However, vaccine effectiveness as an outcome has not been investigated. This study assessed whether maternal PFAS concentrations during pregnancy modified childhood vaccine effectiveness. We analyzed mother-child pairs from the Japan Environment and Children's Study. Children's vaccination status for varicella, mumps, and influenza was collected via...

item.title: Association of TP53 Truncating Mutations with Time to Treatment Failure after First-Line Chemoimmunotherapy in HER2-Mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: TP53 truncating mutations were associated with shorter TTF during first-line pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum in HER2-mutant NSCLC, without significant differences in overall survival or objective response rate. These findings suggest a potential association with shorter treatment durability and require validation in independent cohorts.

item.title: Dietary energy and protein intake assessed based on meal intake rate at dialysis initiation might be associated with 2-year mortality and hospitalization
item.description: CONCLUSION: DEI and DPI, as calculated using data of meal intake rates, are associated independently with 2-year mortality and hospitalization in patients starting dialysis. Patients with unplanned dialysis initiation and with pre-frail or frail condition should be prioritized for nutritional assessment.

item.title: Sex differences in the association between corrected serum calcium and sudden death in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis: ten-year outcomes of the Q-cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Lower corrected serum Ca was associated with higher sudden death risk primarily in women. Sex may modify the prognostic significance of corrected serum Ca for sudden death risk stratification.

item.title: The coexistence of constipation and diarrhea is associated with the development of chronic kidney disease: a 10-year cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The coexistence of constipation and diarrhea is independently associated with an increased risk for the development of CKD. The bowel habit subtype provides clinically relevant information regarding future risk for CKD.

item.title: Adjuvant treatment intensity in circulating tumour DNA-negative colorectal cancer: a systematic review and reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not support omission or broad de-escalation of adjuvant therapy solely because postoperative ctDNA is negative. The association with treatment intensity depended on the type of contrast, complete omission has been examined only in non-randomised data, and absolute differences were small. Research registration PROSPERO registration number: CRD420251153449.

item.title: Association of annual household income and insomnia symptoms based on work-life balance among Japanese female workers in older adult care services: A cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Improving work-life balance may help mitigate insomnia symptoms regardless of income, while low income was associated with a higher prevalence of insomnia symptoms.

item.title: Predictive factors associated with interval changes in STN-DBS lead-tip position between immediate and delayed postoperative CT
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Intracranial air volume was consistently associated with anterior STN-DBS lead-tip displacement between immediate and delayed postoperative CT. Intraoperative head position was also associated with anterior displacement after adjustment for intracranial air volume, although this finding was of borderline statistical significance and should be considered exploratory. These findings support efforts to minimize intracranial air entry during DBS implantation, while the potential...

item.title: Digitalization of the diabetic eye notebook: patient and physician perspectives on a smartphone application for diabetic retinopathy management
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study identified key expectations and concerns among patients and physicians regarding the digitalization of the Diabetic Eye Notebook. Although the application has the potential to overcome practical limitations of the paper-based format, usability for older adults and data security remain major challenges, underscoring the need for further refinement and prospective evaluation.

item.title: Development of a smartphone-based retinal imaging device for stable fundus imaging
item.description: CONCLUSION: The device demonstrates significantly improved stability and ease of use compared with conventional methods. Its design may help reduce operator dependency and facilitate fundus image acquisition in supine patients. Further validation in the intended clinical populations is warranted.

item.title: Comparison of PMAneo and RAPID in acute ischemic stroke: agreement in CT perfusion analysis and DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility
item.description: CONCLUSION: PMAneo showed high volumetric agreement and comparable DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility to RAPID, suggesting it is a reliable alternative for automated CTP analysis. Although proportional bias and potential diagnostic discrepancies were observed in borderline cases near clinically relevant thresholds, PMAneo may facilitate broader access to automated CTP analysis.

item.title: ST20 Staphylococcus aureus causing suppurative cervical lymphadenitis in an extremely low-birth-weight infant
item.description: Neonatal suppurative cervical lymphadenitis is uncommon, particularly in extremely low-birth-weight infants. We report a 772 g infant born at 28 weeks of gestation who developed rapidly progressive unilateral cervical lymphadenitis caused by methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) on postnatal day 31. The infant remained afebrile and blood cultures were negative despite progression requiring repeated drainage. The cervical isolate was genotyped as ST20/spa-t3929 and shared an...

item.title: Emerging roles of OSM and EDA2R-NIK signalling in cancer-associated muscle wasting
item.description: Cancer-associated cachexia (CAC) is a multifactorial metabolic syndrome characterized by progressive skeletal muscle wasting that reduces physical function, compromises treatment tolerance, and contributes to cancer-related mortality. Although systemic inflammation is a major driver of CAC, the mechanisms through which circulating inflammatory signals are translated into muscle-specific catabolic programmes remain incompletely understood. Recent studies have identified oncostatin M (OSM), a...

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Brief Report: Reassessment of bTMB as a Predictive Biomarker in NSCLC Immunotherapy-A Reanalysis of OAK and POPLAR
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The predictiveness of bTMB in identifying patients with NSCLC who may benefit from immunotherapy was evident for PFS but not for OS. Observing a differential treatment efficacy trend solely within the high-bTMB group across multiple cut points was insufficient to establish predictive utility. A valid assessment requires a comprehensive evaluation of both high- and low-bTMB populations, with predictiveness established by reporting differential treatment efficacy between these two...

item.title: Association of reproductive factors with acute myocardial infarction in young women: A VIRGO and NHANES case-control study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Reproductive factors are associated with early-onset AMI in young women. Recognition of reproductive history may inform prevention strategies in young women.

item.title: Selective mGlu<sub>1</sub> Receptor Activation Restores Cortical Inhibitory Tone and Improves Cognitive Performance in a Subchronic Phencyclidine NMDA Hypofunction Model
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify SST-IN-expressed mGlu(1) receptors as critical regulators of prefrontal cortical inhibition and cognition. Positive allosteric modulation of mGlu(1) represents a promising therapeutic strategy for treating cognitive deficits associated with schizophrenia by restoring inhibitory circuit function.

item.title: Delayed elective nodal irradiation in head-and-neck cancer radiotherapy reduces acute lymphocyte damage, lymphopenia, and modulates immune signatures
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that delaying elective nodal irradiation may help preserve circulating immune cells during radiotherapy and provide a mechanistic rationale for future prospective studies evaluating whether this strategy can enhance radiotherapy-immunotherapy synergy in LA-HNSCC.

item.title: GATA-3 identifies a distinct subset of T-PLL associated with skin involvement and CCR4 expression
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Intratumoral and Peritumoral Functional Connectivity Reveals Network-Level Signatures of Glioma
item.description: Gliomas are recognized as network-level diseases that remodel functional connectivity across the brain. Using resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) data from 306 patients with pathologically confirmed glioma at two hospitals, we delineated individualized intra- and peritumoral functional networks to quantify tumor-related alterations. Two novel indices-the ratio of intratumoral functional regions (RIFR) and ratio of peritumoral tumor-related regions (RPTR)-were proposed to describe network...

item.title: Gypsum-calcium carbonate-gelatine composite graft for bone repair: Biocompatibility and histological assessment in a rat model
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Modification of gypsum with calcium carbonate-gelatine hydrogel preserved biocompatibility while reducing degradation rate and promoting more advanced bone regeneration, suggesting POPHD as a promising synthetic bone graft substitute warranting further long-term investigation.

item.title: Global variations, temporal trends, and socioeconomic inequalities in the burden of malignant brain and central nervous system tumors: a population-based systematic analysis of GLOBOCAN 2024
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: We found significant heterogeneity in the incidence, mortality, and lifetime risk of brain and CNS tumors among geographic and HDI levels, which potentially reflects disparities in medical resource allocation and genetic exposures.

item.title: Revolutionizing drought defense: The water-plant-microbe synergy in climate-smart agriculture
item.description: Global warming-induced water scarcity threatens agricultural sustainability. While precision irrigation and microbial inoculants are recognized as effective individual strategies, their synergistic potential remains under-explored. This review synthesizes recent advances in the "water-plant-microbe" synergy to propose a bidirectional regulatory mechanism for climate-smart agriculture. We demonstrate that irrigation regimes function as a primary filter for rhizosphere microbial assembly, thereby...

item.title: Insights Into RP2-Associated Retinopathy: From Molecular Basis to Clinical Translation
item.description: Pathogenic variants in RP2 cause X-linked RP2-associated retinopathy, a rare inherited retinal disorder typically characterized by childhood onset and progression to severe visual impairment within the first three decades of life. Despite its clinical severity, comprehensive clinical and genetic data on RP2-associated retinopathy remain limited and no therapeutic approaches have yet progressed toward clinical application. Here, we provide an overview of current molecular, clinical, and...

item.title: Coronary artery disease polygenic risk score and recurrent cardiovascular events after coronary artery revascularization: A UK Biobank analysis
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Multimodal Imaging of Fundus Abnormalities in Stickler Syndrome: Characterization of 15 Distinct Features Using Ultra-Widefield Swept-Source OCT Angiography
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study used UWF SS-OCTA to systematically characterize fundus phenotypes of Stickler syndrome. Among the 15 identified features, vitreous abnormalities were the most prevalent. We provide in vivo imaging evidence that vitreous anchoring may be a key trigger for retinal breaks and detachment in Stickler syndrome, likely acting through vitreoretinal traction. Its concealment beneath the vitreous fibrous strands may offer a potential theoretical basis for improving targeted...

item.description: No abstract

item.title: Larval habitat characteristics and physicochemical associations of culicine mosquito assemblages in Hormozgan Province, southern Iran
item.description: Understanding the ecological characteristics of mosquito larval habitats is essential for effective vector surveillance and control. This study investigated larval habitat characteristics, water physicochemical properties, and culicine mosquito assemblages in Hormozgan Province, southern Iran. A cross-sectional survey was conducted from September 2016 to April 2017 across four counties representing diverse ecological conditions. Larvae were collected from natural and artificial aquatic habitats...

item.title: Enhancing Proliferation and Pluripotency in Human Dental Pulp Stem Cells through 980-nm Laser Irradiation: Implications for Regenerative Dentistry
item.description: Introduction: Dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) possess remarkable proliferative ability and multilineage differentiation potential, and they are known as immunomodulatory cells. Identifying factors that enhance DPSC proliferation is crucial, as accelerated expansion is necessary for tissue engineering applications, while maintaining pluripotency gene expression is essential to preserve their proliferative and differentiation potential. Low-level laser irradiation (LLLI) has increasingly been...

item.title: An inverse-protein-folding pre-trained model for predicting the mutational effects in protein-protein interactions
item.description: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are fundamental to vast biological processes. Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in PPIs is crucial for protein engineering and drug discovery. Most existing PPI prediction approaches rely on refined physicochemical features or computationally intensive structural sampling. Here, we present delta-G message-passing-neural-network (DGMPNN), a message-passing neural-network framework for predicting the effects of mutations on PPIs. DGMPNN is...

item.title: Association of dual-pathway antithrombotic therapy with primary patency after iliofemoral venous stenting: a multicenter cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Primary patency after iliofemoral venous stenting was similarly high with dual-pathway antithrombotic therapy and AC alone. An exploratory analysis suggested a possible association between AC+APT and improved patency in patients with post-thrombotic syndrome. Adequately powered randomized trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm this finding and assess long-term safety.

item.title: Combination of live-attenuated and adenovirus-based vaccines provides immediate and durable protection against Yersinia pestis in mice
item.description: Yersinia pestis is the etiological agent of pandemic-causing plague with no Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved vaccines. The natural emergence or intentional release of antimicrobial-resistant strains are alarming, necessitating development of new-generation vaccines and immunization strategies that produce rapid and durable immunity. Herein, we evaluated immediate (within 7 days) or long-term (6 months) protection and immune responses by combining patented live-attenuated vaccines...

item.title: Type 2 diabetes mellitus and risk of incident peptic ulcer disease: a large-scale prospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Baseline T2DM was associated with a higher risk of incident PUD and its anatomical subtypes. Residual confounding, selection and detection biases, and the lack of systematic Helicobacter pylori data preclude causal interpretation.

item.title: Clinical Characteristics and Predictors of Mortality in Elderly Patients with Bloodstream Infections: A 12-Year Retrospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged invasive medical interventions, including mechanical ventilation, central venous catheterization, and urinary catheterization, as well as chemotherapy or radiotherapy, were independently associated with higher mortality in elderly BSI patients. These findings highlight the need for risk-stratified management strategies to optimize outcomes in these elderly patients.

item.title: Virtual Diabetes Optimization Program (VDOP) for Veterans With Uncontrolled Diabetes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: VDOP was associated with greater improvements in glycemic control and weight loss compared with standard endocrine care. Prospective studies are needed to assess long-term outcomes and cost-effectiveness.

item.title: Cumulative Sonographic Features From the Morphological Uterus Sonographic Assessment (MUSA) System and Clinical Severity of Adenomyosis in Congolese Women: A Multicenter Study in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A higher cumulative MUSA feature count was associated with severe chronic pelvic pain, with the association mainly driven by indirect sonographic features. Cumulative MUSA feature count should be considered an exploratory phenotypic measure rather than a validated severity score. Prospective external validation using standardized image acquisition and independent blinded readers is warranted.

item.title: Acceptability and Feasibility of a Primary Care Hypoglycemia Prevention Program: A Pilot Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A hypoglycemia prevention program designed for primary care is feasible to implement and acceptable to clinical and patient stakeholders, with evidence of improved hypoglycemia prevention efforts. Further efficacy evaluation is needed.

item.title: Candidate place-based factors before and after composite allocation score implementation in lung transplantation in the United States
item.description: BACKGROUND: In March 2023, the Composite Allocation Score (CAS) and continuous distribution replaced the Lung Allocation Score (LAS) for lung transplantation in the United States in part to reduce the role of geography. We examined whether ZIP-code-level socioeconomic drivers of waitlisted patients were associated with time to transplant or waitlist attrition, defined as death or removal due to being too sick.

item.title: Assessing the Potential Distribution of Eriocheir sinensis Under Climate Change: Regional Contrasts and Spatial Mismatches in Terrestrial and Nearshore Suitability
item.description: The Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis), native to China and the Korean Peninsula, has established invasive populations with substantial ecological and economic impacts in Europe and North America. Anticipating changes in its potential distribution is important for invasion-risk screening and estuarine management. item.title: Chlorin e6 as a Photosensitizer for Inducing Targeted Effects in Transscleral Photodynamic Therapy
item.description: Introduction: This study aimed to evaluate the role of chlorin e6 in mediating targeted vascular injury during transscleral photodynamic therapy (TS-PDT) under controlled thermal conditions. Methods: Twenty eyes of ten rabbits were randomized into two groups. The TS-PDT group received intravenous chlorin e6 (2.5 mg/kg) followed by transscleral laser irradiation (660 nm, 0.17 W, 10 min.). The control group (TSLT) underwent identical laser exposure without a photosensitizer. Scleral temperature...

item.title: Iturin A disrupts Cryptococcus neoformans membrane integrity, attenuates virulence, and synergizes with amphotericin B
item.description: Cryptococcus neoformans is a major fungal pathogen with severely limited therapeutic options. We evaluated the antifungal activity of the lipopeptide iturin A against eight clinical isolates of C. neoformans. Iturin A exhibited robust anti-cryptococcal activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations ranging from 12.5 to 25 μg/mL, and demonstrated minimal toxicity in A549 lung epithelial cells and HepG2/C3A liver cells. Combination treatment with amphotericin B was synergistic (fractional...

item.title: Shifting dominance: bilingual language skills in Spanish-English bilinguals' English reading comprehension over time
item.description: This longitudinal study investigated the relative importance of various bilingual language skills predictors for English reading comprehension over time in Spanish-English bilingual children in elementary grades. We examined the contributions of phonological awareness (PA), morphological awareness (MA), syntactic awareness (SA), and vocabulary in both English and Spanish at two time points. Dominance analysis was used to examine the shifting pattern of relative contributions of bilingual...

item.title: Comparable Norovirus Shedding in Symptomatic and Asymptomatic Individuals: A Hospital-Based Study in Bangladesh
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Norovirus shedding quantity and duration were similar between AGE cases and asymptomatic controls, complicating the attribution of norovirus infection to AGE in Bangladesh. Larger longitudinal studies would more accurately characterize norovirus shedding in resource-limited settings.

item.title: The effectiveness of sound-based interventions on promoting sleep quality in hospitalized patients: A systematic review
item.description: Sleep quality strongly affects hospitalized patients' recovery, yet pain, anxiety, and environmental factors such as noise and light frequently disrupt it. Sound-based therapies offer a promising, non-pharmacological approach, but their effectiveness has not been comprehensively synthesized. This systematic review examined fifteen studies (2012-2026, 2024 patients, mostly intensive care settings) evaluating sound-based interventions, including calming music, nature sounds, and white noise, on...

item.title: Estimation of Antimicrobial-Resistant Mycoplasma genitalium Infections in People Aged 14-59 Years: Results From the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, United States, 2017-2018
item.description: Mycoplasma genitalium antimicrobial resistance is common in US sexual health clinics. Population-level prevalence is unknown. We tested National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2017-2018) specimens for M genitalium resistance mutations (n = 58). Macrolide resistance prevalence was 42.7% (95% CI, 24.4%-62.7%). Quinolone resistance was not detected. Macrolide resistance testing should guide azithromycin treatment.

item.title: Culinary Medicine and Medical Nutrition Therapy Interventions to Improve Glycemic Control in Type 2 Diabetes: A Pragmatic Trial During the COVID-19 Pandemic
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Despite the impact of COVID-19, participants in the diverse-format MNT intervention had clinically meaningful improvements in HbA(1c) at 6 months. Unmet recruitment and retention goals contributed to underpowered results. Additional RCTs evaluating the impact of CM on glycemic control and dietary measures are needed.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Partnered status, older age, hypertension, neuropathy, and interval severe hypoglycemia predicted 1-year cognitive decline detectable with brief cognitive screening and processing speed measures, underscoring the importance of cognitive assessment and monitoring in older adults with T1D who present with these risk factors.

item.title: Differential Associations Between Diabetes Distress Subtypes and Diabetes-Dependent Quality of Life and the Buffering Effect of Online Support Among Young Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: A Cross-sectional Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings revealed the differential associations between diabetes distress subtypes and DDQoL and the moderating role of online support in reducing the negative impact of interpersonal distress, underscoring the need for interventions targeting emotional distress and optimizing online support for young adults with T1D.

item.description: The "Race for the Surface" hypothesis remains the dogma for explaining the competition between host proteins, cells, and bacteria for implant colonization immediately post-op. Recently, we used intravital microscopy to provide direct evidence supporting this hypothesis by demonstrating that the race for the surface in a murine implant-associated infection (IAI) model is complete within 3 h. However, this intravital imaging is impractical for early-stage drug development research, thus warranting...

item.title: Engineering uORFs in wheat improves abiotic stress tolerance without growth penalties
item.description: Developing climate-resilient crops is critical for ensuring global food security, yet agricultural productivity is frequently constrained by the trade-off between stress tolerance and growth. This challenge is particularly acute in allohexaploid wheat, a staple crop susceptible to abiotic stresses, underscoring the demand for precise gene regulation. Here, we established a simple, efficient, and transgene-free method for regulating gene expression in allohexaploid wheat by disrupting or creating...

item.title: Cell-type-specific PIN-FORMED 3-mediated polar auxin transport regulates cambial activity and tension wood formation in Populus tomentosa
item.description: Auxin is a central regulator of tree secondary growth and forms maxima in the vascular cambium, yet how these maxima are established remains elusive. Here, we functionally characterized two redundant PIN-FORMED 3 (PIN3) paralogs from Populus tomentosa to define their roles in secondary growth and gravity-induced tension wood (TW) formation. item.title: Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles
item.description: Cardiac re-entrant arrhythmias are a major cause of sudden cardiac death. Optogenetic defibrillation has emerged as a promising anti-arrhythmic strategy based on photoactivation of channelrhodopsins, yet the efficacy and potential adverse consequences of activating different classes of light-gated ion channels have not been systematically evaluated. Previous studies assessed either cation (e.g. ChR2) or anion (e.g. GtACR1) non-selective channels, both of which depolarize resting cardiomyocytes....

item.title: Plagiarism and duplicate publications in the medical literature: scope of the problem, risks, warning signs, and prevention strategies
item.description: Plagiarism and duplicate publications pose a persistent threat to the integrity and credibility of the medical literature. Despite the widespread adoption of ethical rules, international guidelines, and detection software, these practices remain prevalent in medical research, and their scope continues to expand. Their consequences extend beyond damaging the reputation of researchers and journals. They can bias the scientific evidence base, distort the outcomes of systematic reviews and...

item.title: Bilateral Breast Gradient Insert Prototype for Strong Diffusion Encoding at 3 T
item.description: CONCLUSION: This work demonstrates a dedicated bilateral breast gradient insert for safe and feasible strong-gradient breast diffusion MRI and represents a first step toward dedicated hardware for breast cancer detection and characterization without contrast agents.

item.title: Programmable Nanozyme Gating: A Molecular Ejector Switch (MES) for High-Fidelity miRNA-21 Sensing
item.description: Nucleotide-level variants in miRNA or pathogen genomes can critically reprogram gene-regulatory networks or enhance disease severity, highlighting the urgent need for sensing platforms capable of resolving subtle sequence discrepancies. In this article, we present a programmable molecular ejector switch (MES) that functions as a confinement-gating smart nanozyme for adaptive nucleic-acid sensing. item.title: Palliative care training for healthcare professionals in ethnic minority regions of China: a qualitative study of training needs, barriers and practice translation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Palliative care training needs and barriers in ethnic minority regions of China extend beyond limited training provision alone. They are shaped by the intersection of structural constraints, inadequate contextual adaptation, and difficulty translating learning into practice. Strengthening training in these settings will require more than expanding course provision; it will require culturally responsive, practice-oriented, and sustained forms of local capacity building. item.title: Statistical methods for analyzing change over time of continuous outcomes in observational health studies: a scoping review of suggested approaches
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The methodological literature provides a diverse set of approaches addressing RTM and ME in analyses of within-person change, but many of these considerations are not routinely reflected in applied observational research. By synthesizing methodological guidance and comparing it with current analytical practice, this review provides a structured framework to support more transparent and methodologically informed analyses of longitudinal change.

item.title: Differences in Office and Ambulatory Pulse Wave Analysis in Patients with White Coat Hypertension and Other Hypertension Phenotypes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In patients with WCE, there are significant differences in arterial stiffness parameters between office and 24h measurements, suggesting that both measurement methods provide complementary hemodynamic information. Prospective studies are needed to determine the prognostic significance of these differences.

item.description: CONCLUSION: MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA is feasible within a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol and supports further clinical translation of radiation-free endovascular treatment.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings are crucial for understanding the mechanisms underlying IBD-associated cancer and developing innovative therapeutic strategies. During the inflammation-cancer transition, activation of the SOX4 leads to increased COL4A1/A2 secretion by CXCL14+ fibroblasts, resulting in enhanced collagen IV synthesis. item.title: IL-1β/IL-6 inflammatory crosstalk drives DNA methylation and histone remodeling associated with cytokine induced senescence in luminal breast cancer
item.description: CONCLUSION: An IL-1β/IL-6 inflammatory loop drives epigenetic remodeling associated with cytokine induced senescence while promoting tumor-supportive signaling. IL-1β initiates the senescence program, whereas IL-6 reinforces and sustains this state through STAT3/DNMT signaling, highlighting inflammatory cytokine signaling pathways as potential therapeutic targets for breast cancer therapy.

item.title: Targeted pathway mining reveals novel modified hexapeptides from the demiguisin family
item.description: Following the discovery of the piperazic acid (Piz)-containing hexapeptide demiguisin A from a toxic bird-associated Amycolatopsis strain, we aimed to investigate the structural diversity and bioactive potential of this natural product family. item.description: Burmese pythons exhibit cardiac remodeling in response to increased metabolic rate during digestion. item.description: Persistent hypertension (HTN) remains common after covered stent implantation for coarctation of the aorta (CoA). item.description: The alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is intrinsically limited by the lack of active hydrogen and sluggish hydrogen transfer. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Lower PAAT is associated with higher risks of death in community-dwelling older adults. The association appears to be explained largely by cardiovascular disease and systemic health status rather than pulmonary disease alone. PAAT may serve as an integrated marker of cardiopulmonary and systemic vulnerability in older adults.

item.description: CONCLUSION: Specific gut microbial profiles may be associated with cardiometabolic markers, particularly obesity-related traits. Future longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the directionality and underlying mechanisms of these associations.

item.description: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) is a progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage destruction, extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation, and chronic inflammation, yet effective disease-modifying therapeutic targets and pharmacological interventions remain limited. item.description: Traumatic memories that are resistant to modification or extinction are a characteristic feature of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). item.description: The prognosis for glioblastoma (GBM) is correlated with the extent of resection. Continuous en bloc resection (CEBR) is a surgical strategy that involves the removal of the gross tumor along with its normal adjacent tissue (NAT) as "one whole block". However, its impact on the survival of patients with GBM in non-eloquent areas is unknown. item.description: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) remains a major cause of cancer mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that remodel metastatic RNA-splicing programs are poorly defined. item.description: INTRODUCTION: Environmental seasonal changes, including allergen exposure, pollutants, and viral prevalence, impact gene expression across human tissues. Therefore, season of sample collection is critical to consider when analyzing disease-associated transcriptional programs. In this study we aimed to investigate the effect of season on identification of asthma-associated genes.

item.description: The ERK/MNK/eIF4E signaling axis is critically involved in cap-dependent translation and significantly impacts survival and chemotherapy resistance in ovarian cancer. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Atypical causal reasoning under uncertainty may constitute a key cognitive mechanism underlying relapse, offering a computational account of how individuals respond to abstinence violations. This work provides a theoretical foundation for developing targeted cognitive-behavioral interventions aimed at reducing relapse risk.

item.title: Acupuncture versus reflexology for cancer-related pain in palliative care: a pragmatic study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Both acupuncture and reflexology were associated with reduced within-group EORTC pain and ESAS and EORTC fatigue and appetite, physical, emotional and social function; only acupuncture with reduction of ESAS pain; and only reflexology improved wellbeing, somnolence and insomnia, with a between-group advantage for EORTC appetite and cognitive function. Further research is needed to confirm the findings within larger and more diverse patient populations.

item.title: Deuterium between 31 and 1021 ppm in dietary water has no effect on lifespan in the adult housefly (Musca domestica)
item.description: Deuterium, an isotope of hydrogen, exists naturally in the environment and body water at around 89-158 ppm. We investigated the lifespan effects in houseflies fed diets made up with a range of deuterium, depleted or enriched relative to natural abundance water (31 ppm to 1021 ppm). item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings revealed that PM(2.5) components (2-year exposure) may be important risk factors for adverse cardiorenal outcomes.

item.title: Genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance for monitoring human norovirus GII circulation
item.description: Norovirus GII causes a substantial global burden of acute gastroenteritis, and genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance offers a complementary approach for monitoring community circulation beyond cases captured by routine clinical surveillance. item.description: The "metal ion hypothesis" of Alzheimer's disease (AD) has gained widespread acceptance, but translating this understanding into effective therapies remains elusive. This likely stems from a simplistic understanding of metal homeostasis as merely a matter of "excess and deficiency." item.description: Amino acid metabolism has emerged as a critical nexus linking tumor cell nutrient acquisition with immune microenvironmental regulation, providing a rich source of druggable targets for cancer therapy. item.title: Transient but not sustained p53 activation by targeting METTL3 prevents radiation-induced intestinal injury through dual-regulation of revival stem cells
item.description: Radiation-induced intestinal injury (RIII) remains a severe complication of radiotherapy. Although p53 activation is known to be protective, no clinically available p53 activators exist. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests a potential contribution of GALNT variants to male infertility and provides the first evidence implicating GALNT3 and GALNT8 variants in human asthenoteratozoospermia. ICSI represents a favorable reproductive strategy for infertile patients carrying GALNT variants.

item.title: Projected burden of cold spell-attributable Parkinson's disease mortality among older adults in China under climate change and population ageing
item.description: Population ageing may amplify cold-related health risks under climate change, particularly for older adults with Parkinson's disease (PD). item.description: Oxidized phospholipids containing phosphatidylcholine (PC-OxPLs), present on oxidized low-density lipoproteins (OxLDL) and apoptotic cells, are pathogenic in osteoporosis. item.description: CONCLUSION: Based on current observational evidence, autologous blood reinfusion during ECMO weaning appears feasible and is associated with favorable surrogate hematological outcomes compared with direct discard. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Subjective and objective cognition showed distinct associations with symptom course, supporting their combined assessment. Better baseline objective memory did not necessarily indicate fewer residual symptoms, but this association does not establish reduced treatment efficacy.

item.title: Altered resting-state EEG microstate dynamics are associated with auditory hallucinations in patients with major depressive disorder
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In first-episode MDD, a lifetime history of auditory hallucination experiences was associated with increased microstate C occurrence. item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Collaborative inpatient PC models for COPD should prioritize addressing common palliative needs, strengthen generalist PC skills, establish clear criteria for specialist PC involvement, and improve coordination across care settings.

item.description: CONCLUSIONS: By integrating statistical feature engineering with deep learning, this framework provides a CBC-based pre-genetic-testing risk-stratification (triage) approach. item.description: Riboflavin is an essential vitamin widely used in pharmaceutical and feed applications, and its industrial production relies primarily on microbial fermentation. item.description: CONCLUSION: Under controlled conditions, mouse blood proteins survive moulting and are passed onto the next developmental stage in I. ricinus ticks, from larvae to nymphs. These proteins are detectable up to five months post-moulting.
